title: Sultanate of Jambi
capsule: The Sultanate of Jambi was a Malay Islamic sultanate centered on the Batang Hari river basin in central Sumatra, whose control of pepper and gold exports from the Minangkabau highlands made it by the 1670s the second-largest Sumatran port after Aceh. Dutch VOC interference from the mid-17th century — including the forcible removal of Sultan Ingalaga in 1688 — split the sultanate into rival Upper and Lower factions whose internal conflicts the Dutch exploited for two centuries, installing puppet rulers from 1858 onward. Sultan Taha Saifuddin refused all Dutch suzerainty and waged guerrilla resistance from the interior for decades; his death in 1904 effectively ended the sultanate's independent existence, and its territory was formally absorbed into the Dutch East Indies residency system in 1905.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's core riverine territory is documented in Dutch colonial records, but the outer extent of its claimed hinterland was contested and only loosely administered.
